video.title: The Fantasy Basketball Sleepers You NEED To Pay Attention To

summary: Josh Lloyd lists fantasy basketball sleepers he thinks are drafted or ranked too late. He uses Yahoo ranks, Yahoo ADP and Fantrax ADP, and skips ESPN because its rankings have not been updated. He covers category leagues first, then Yahoo points leagues. His main targets are players he sees as discounted for risk: Anthony Davis, Kyrie Irving, Darius Garland, Paul George, Dejounte Murray, Brandon Miller, Dyson Daniels, Ausar Thompson, Coby White and Day'Ron Sharpe. For points leagues he adds Paolo Banchero, Stephon Castle, Jaylen Brown, Deni Avdija, Domantas Sabonis, Rudy Gobert and CJ McCollum. His central argument is that a big gap between a player's price and his expected finish protects you even if the player falls short.

rules.text: Look for large gaps between ADP and expected value, not small ones. A gap of a few spots leaves little margin for error. A gap of 15 to 20 spots protects you even if the player underperforms.
rules.quote: If he's 40th and I think he's 24th, well, even if he doesn't live up to my expectation, I got a big gap

rules.text: ADP is an average and can mislead. A median draft position would be more useful. An ADP of 46 means the player goes outside the top 50 in some leagues.
rules.quote: I do wish they would do an MDP, a median draft position. I think that would probably give us better results

rules.text: Players with injury or age risk can be good value when the discount is large enough, because the risk is already priced in.
rules.quote: this is a middle of the second round sort of a player. We're already baking in three rounds of value here.

rules.text: If you do not want to punt free throws, do not draft Giannis at all. Fantrax ADPs mix formats and can be distorted.
rules.quote: I don't want to punt free throws then don't take him like at all. Don't take him at nine.

rules.text: Assists are scarce in the middle rounds. Hybrid guards who can get 4 to 6 assists are worth targeting there.
rules.quote: Getting a high assist player at this point in the draft is difficult. And all of these guys could get five, six.

rules.text: Steals are volatile game to game, week to week and year to year. Good steals players still keep providing value over time.
rules.quote: The Steels are a tough category. They vary game to game, week to week, year to year a lot.

rules.text: Late in drafts, target functional centers who provide cheap rebounds and blocks.
rules.quote: when you're looking for a functional center around that spot, functional microwave cover, easy.

rules.text: Small differences at the top of a draft matter more than small differences later on.
rules.quote: the pointy end of a draft it is it is important those small differences at the top.

rules.text: Yahoo ranks and ADP are format agnostic. Players who are much better in points leagues than in category leagues can be big points league values.
rules.quote: Remembering that Yahoo ranks and ADPs are format agnostic. They don't care that you're in a points league or a category league.

rules.text: Learn how a site presents its information and how player value differs across formats. You can gain value from the gaps.
rules.quote: understanding how a player differs in different formats and how you can split the gaps on that is a great way

rules.text: A risky late pick that fails does not ruin a draft when the upside is high.
rules.quote: Let's say you pick him at 80 and he plays 20 games. Does that kill your draft? No.
